title: A publishing CEO names it one of two books she hand-sold this year — 'I must have recommended to 3 dozen people'
summary: Pierucci's post is about why most books never sell: a Pareto distribution so steep that an entire YA category dropped 25% in a half-year because Suzanne Collins did not publish. Her prescription is that the only reliable route is a book readers pass on themselves. She names two she personally drove this year, and Incorruptible is one of them — an estimate of three dozen recommendations from someone whose profession is knowing how books actually spread.
blockquote: This year I recommended the bejeezus out of "Theo of Golden," but another book I honestly assisted greatly with sales was Eric Ries's "Incorruptible," which I must have recommended to 3 dozen people.
attribution_title: 2-time WSJ bestselling writer · publishing company CEO
